transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I've been struggling a lot with constant fidgeting lately. I just can't seem to keep my hands and feet still, and I'm always tapping them or squirming in my seat. It's getting really hard to manage, so I wanted to get some help with it.
Do you also have difficulty paying attention to details, following instructions, or making careless mistakes in your daily activities or when working on tasks?

Yes, I have a really hard time following through on instructions and often fail to finish my chores or work tasks. I'll start something but just can't seem to get to the finish line. As for making careless mistakes, I'm not really sure about that.
Can you think of any specific situations where you had trouble paying attention or made mistakes due to not paying attention, such as in school, work, or personal projects?

At work, I often get halfway through a task or project but fail to finish it because I struggle to follow through on the instructions. People in my life, like my family and coworkers, also get frustrated with me because they feel I'm not listening when they speak directly to me.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with fidgeting, following instructions, and completing tasks?
I've been dealing with these struggles for about a year and two months now. It has been a pretty consistent issue for me during that entire time.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking, blurt out answers before questions are finished, or have difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations or activities?
No, I don't really experience those issues. I haven't noticed myself interrupting others or having trouble waiting my turn in conversations.
Can you describe any situations where you felt excessively restless, had difficulty engaging in quiet leisure activities, or felt like you were 'on the go' or 'driven by a motor'?

Yes, I definitely feel excessively restless a lot of the time. I frequently experience this intense inner restlessness and an urge to stay active, which makes it really hard for me to just sit still and relax during quiet moments.

Yes, I have a really hard time following through on instructions and often leave my chores or work tasks unfinished. I'll start them but just can't seem to complete them. As for making careless mistakes, I'm not really sure about that.
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking, blurt out answers before questions are finished, or have difficulty waiting for your turn in conversations or activities?
No, I don't really have trouble with those things. I don't find myself interrupting people, blurting out answers, or struggling to wait my turn.
Do you think your difficulties with restlessness and fidgeting, or your difficulties with following instructions and completing tasks, cause you more problems in your daily life?

I'm not really sure which one causes more problems because both are very challenging for me in my daily life. I haven't really compared them before, as they both make things quite difficult in their own ways.
I'm sorry, but I didn't quite catch what you just said. Could you please repeat that for me?

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of constant fidgeting, difficulty following instructions, and completing tasks are consistent with both Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) and Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation). However, the patient's report of excessive restlessness and feeling 'on the go' or 'driven by a motor' suggests that they may also be experiencing hyperactive symptoms, which is more characteristic of the Combined Presentation. The patient's denial of interrupting others, blurting out answers, or having difficulty waiting for their turn suggests that the Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation is less likely. Since the patient's symptoms have been consistent for over a year, it is likely that the disorder is persistent, but more information is needed to confirm the diagnosis.

Further questioning is needed to determine the predominant type of symptoms and to rule out other potential diagnoses.
